what_happened: The person running Athena lifted the scope pause on line 5389 by hand. Two attempts on that line (5389 and jz9t) had stopped in planning at round 3, spending $4.75 against a $3.20 forecast. The stated causes were an insufficient budget and unproven test seams. Both causes are already fixed by landed jobs d6y1 and 3jat. Meanwhile Hestia had re-queued the line's root-cause request four times (gdgv, 7ym7, 487a, 2hc1). Each copy hit the pause and stopped a drain. The lift lets the request run once, and the scope guard can pause the line again if spend repeats. No job failed. This was an intervention that overrode the scope guard's pause.
cause: The drain treats every queued item as runnable and never checks whether the item's line is paused. The re-queuer also does not record that a request already stopped a drain, so it files the same request again. Nothing retires, holds or revalidates queued items on a paused line. A pause is also not tied to the fixes for its cause, so the pause stays in force after the fixes land. One paused line therefore produces repeated drain stops until a person lifts the pause or closes items.
prevention: Two code checks together. (1) The drain skips and leaves untouched any item whose line is paused. It records the skip and shows it in status, so a paused line cannot stop a drain. (2) The re-queuer refuses to enqueue a request while an identical or same-line request is queued or the line is paused. Separately, when a job lands that is named as a fix for a paused line's cause, Athena flags the pause for review. That flag lets a pause be lifted by a recorded step instead of an unplanned hand intervention.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain and the re-queuer respect paused lines. Outcome: (1) When the drain meets a queued item whose line is paused by the scope guard, it skips the item without running it and without counting a failure. It leaves the item queued, and it reports the skip and the pause reason in the drain output and in `athena status`. A paused line never stops a drain. (2) The re-queuer (Hestia) does not enqueue a request when an identical request, or any request on the same paused line, is already queued, or when the line is paused. It records the refusal with the reason. (3) When a job lands that a pause note names as the fix for the line's cause, `athena status` shows that the pause is ready for review and names the landed job. Acceptance: a test with a paused line holding three queued items shows the drain finishing the other items, the paused-line items still queued and reported, and no drain stop. A test shows a re-queue attempt for a paused line is refused with a recorded reason. A test shows the review flag appearing once the named fix job has landed. Use realistic queue records written by the real writers, not hand-built fixtures. Check any text added to prompts or docs against the banned-word list.
